Fragmenta in epistulam i ad Thessalonicenses (in catenis)
1 Thess: Prolog
Πολλοὺς ὑπέμειναν διωγμοὺς οἱ ἐν Θεσσαλονίκῃ Χριστιανοὶ οἱ ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν
πιστεύσαντες ὑπὸ τῶν ἔτι Ἑλλήνων ὄντων, ἐφ' οἷς αὐτοὺς παραμυθεῖται. μέμνηται
δὲ καὶ τῆς τῶν νεκρῶν ἀναστάσεως παραμυθούμενος αὐτοὺς ἐν ταῖς τῶν οἰκείων
ἀποβολαῖς. ἡ δὲ προτεταγμένη τοῦ προοιμίου εὐχαριστία τῷ θεῷ μαρτυρία ἐστὶ τῆς
τῶν Θεσσαλονικέων εὐλαβείας. 1 Thess 1,3 Ἡ μὲν πίστις ἐγείρει πρὸς ἔργον τοῦ
ἀγαθοῦ, ἡ δὲ ἀγάπη παραμένειν ποιεῖ τοῖς πόνοις, ἡ δὲ ἐλπὶς ὑπομένειν ποιεῖ μετὰ
μακροθυμίας τοὺς ἀγωνιζομένους. Καὶ ἡ μὲν πίστις ἐγείρει πρὸς καμάτους, ἡ δὲ
ἀγάπη ἐπιμένειν ποιεῖ τοῖς πόνοις. 329 1 Thess 1,4®5 Εἰδότες, φησίν, ἀδελφοὶ
ἠγαπημένοι, ὅτι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον οὐκ ἐγενήθη εἰς ὑμᾶς ἐν λόγῳ μόνῳ, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν
δυνάμει. οὐ μόνον, φησίν, ἐκηρύξαμεν ὑμῖν τὸν λόγον, ἀλλὰ καὶ δυνάμεις καὶ
θαυματουργίας ὑμῖν ἐπεδείξαμεν. 1 Thess 1,8 Ἀντὶ τοῦ διαδίδοται καὶ διαβεβόηται. 1
Thess 2,2 Οὐκ ἀφείλετο ἡμῶν, φησί, τὰ ἐν Φιλίπποις κακὰ τὴν εἰς Χριστὸν
παρρησίαν, ἀλλ' ἐλθόντες πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἀδεῶς ἐκηρύξαμεν τὸν λόγον. 1 Thess 2,4 Τὸ
εὐαγγέλιον δι' οὗ παρακαλοῦμεν τοὺς θλιβομένους, τοῦτ' ἔστιν ἡ ἀνάστασις καὶ ἡ ἐν
αὐτῇ μισθαποδοσία οὐ κατὰ πλάνην ἀλλὰ κατ' ἀλήθειαν κηρύττεται. 1 Thess 2,7
Ἀντὶ τοῦ ἐπιβαρεῖς καὶ ἐπαχθεῖς διὰ τὸ ἀπαιτεῖν τιμὰς ἃς δεῖ τιμᾶσθαι ἀποστόλους
Χριστοῦ.
thought_title: Paul's comfort and thanksgiving for the Thessalonians
orientation: Severianus opens his commentary by describing the situation of the Thessalonian Christians and Paul's purpose in writing to them.
pass_a_gloss: Many persecutions endured the Christians in Thessalonica, the ones from the Gentiles who believed, under those still being Greeks, on account of which things he comforts them. He also mentions the resurrection of the dead, comforting them in the losses of their relatives. The thanksgiving placed before the preface is a testimony to God of the piety of the Thessalonians. The faith rouses toward work of the good, the love makes to remain in the labors, the hope makes to endure with patience those who struggle. And the faith rouses toward toils, the love makes to remain in the labors. Knowing, he says, brothers beloved by God, that the gospel did not come to you in word only, but also in power. Not only, he says, did we preach the word to you, but also powers and wonder-workings we displayed to you. Instead of 'it is spread abroad and noised abroad.' The evils in Philippi, he says, did not take away our boldness toward Christ, but coming to you we preached the word without fear. The gospel through which we comfort those who are afflicted, that is the resurrection and the reward-giving in it, is preached not according to error but according to truth. Instead of burdensome and oppressive because of demanding honors which apostles of Christ ought to be honored with.

choices.english: the ones from the Gentiles who believed
choices.why: Keeps the participle force and the source phrase 'from the Gentiles' as a defining group
rejected: those who believed from among the nations

choices.why: Preserves the present participle 'being' and the temporal force of 'still'
rejected: by those who were still Greeks
at the hands of those still Greek

choices.why: The passive participle is rendered with its implied agent, matching the brief's instruction to avoid hyphenated compounds
Literal rendering of the dative with 'only' as adverb

choices.english: it is spread abroad and noised abroad
choices.why: Both verbs are passive and describe the spread of the gospel's fame; kept as two coordinated passives
Both adjectives describe the weight of demanding honors; kept as a pair

pass_b_english: The Christians in Thessalonica, the ones from the Gentiles who believed, endured many persecutions under those still being Greeks, and Paul comforts them for these things. He also mentions the resurrection of the dead, comforting them in the losses of their relatives. The thanksgiving to God placed before the opening is a testimony to the piety of the Thessalonians.

Faith rouses a person toward the work of the good, love makes them remain in their labors, and hope makes those who struggle endure with patience. Faith rouses them toward toils, and love makes them remain in their labors.

Paul says, “You know, brothers beloved by God, that the gospel did not come to you in word only, but also in power” (1 Thessalonians 1:4-5). He means: we did not only preach the word to you, but we also displayed powers and wonder-workings to you.
On “your faith has gone forth” (1 Thessalonians 1:8), he means: it is spread abroad and noised abroad.
Paul says, “The evils at Philippi did not take away our boldness toward Christ, but when we came to you we preached the word without fear” (1 Thessalonians 2:2).
The gospel through which we comfort the afflicted—that is, the resurrection and the reward-giving in it—is preached not according to error but according to truth (1 Thessalonians 2:4).
On “we were able to be burdensome” (1 Thessalonians 2:7), he means: burdensome and oppressive, because of demanding the honors with which the apostles of Christ ought to be honored.

last_rejected.quote: Paul says, “You know, brothers beloved by God”
last_rejected.why: English adds 'by God' not in source; makes Paul say what Severianus didn't quote, confusing speaker boundary.
last_rejected.ruling: ἠγαπημένοι implies 'beloved by God' (cf. 1 Thess 1:4); standard biblical idiom, not a misleading addition.

last_rejected.why: 'Wonder-workings' is not natural English; source means 'miracles' or 'wonders,' not the act of working wonders.
last_rejected.ruling: θαυματουργίας = 'wonder-workings'; acceptable rendering within normal range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: The evils at Philippi did not take away our boldness toward Christ
last_rejected.source_quote: Οὐκ ἀφείλετο ἡμῶν, φησί, τὰ ἐν Φιλίπποις κακὰ τὴν εἰς Χριστὸν παρρησίαν
last_rejected.why: 'toward Christ' misrepresents εἰς Χριστόν which means 'in Christ' or 'for Christ'; agency of boldness is changed.
last_rejected.ruling: εἰς Χριστόν can mean 'toward Christ'; within normal range, not a clear mistranslation.

last_rejected.quote: we were able to be burdensome
last_rejected.why: English 'able to be' adds capability not in source; Greek explains ἐπιβαρεῖς as 'burdensome and oppressive'.
last_rejected.ruling: English quotes 1 Thess 2:7 ('we were able to be burdensome'), not the Greek scholion; source ἐπιβαρεῖς = 'burdensome' correctly glossed.

last_rejected.quote: because of demanding the honors with which the apostles of Christ ought to be honored
last_rejected.source_quote: διὰ τὸ ἀπαιτεῖν τιμὰς ἃς δεῖ τιμᾶσθαι ἀποστόλους Χριστοῦ
last_rejected.why: 'with which...ought to be honored' distorts syntax; ἃς δεῖ τιμᾶσθαι ἀποστόλους Χριστοῦ = 'which apostles of Christ ought to receive'.
last_rejected.fix: because of demanding the honors that apostles of Christ ought to receive
last_rejected.ruling: τιμᾶσθαι is passive 'be honored'; English correctly renders ἃς δεῖ τιμᾶσθαι ἀποστόλους Χριστοῦ as honors apostles ought to receive.
